# double-meh

> A modern, fetch-native HTTP I/O library for browsers and CLIs (Node, Bun, Deno) — a thin, DX-first layer over `fetch()`. The method declares the return shape; options tune behavior, never shape. Composable services (in-flight dedup, app-governed cache, verb-aware retry, serverless mocking, request bundling), web-native streaming in both directions, parsed record iteration, and a reconnecting SSE client. REST correctness (conditional writes, idempotency keys, `problem+json`, content negotiation) is a per-call one-liner. Zero runtime dependencies, ESM-only, hand-written TypeScript typings.

## Install

npm i double-meh

ESM-only. CJS consumers can `require('double-meh')` on Node >= 20.19 (`require(esm)`); the module graph carries no top-level await, which is what keeps that path synchronous.

No build step is required in a browser: vendor `src` and map the package with two import-map entries, `"double-meh"` to `index.js` and `"double-meh/"` to the folder — one prefix covers every subpath because the wildcard does not transform. The full entry is 18 modules and 3 graph levels; verbs alone (`io.js` plus `transports/fetch.js`) are 4 modules, which is smaller over the wire than the whole entry bundled and minified.

## Quick start

```js
import io from 'double-meh';

const person = await io.get('https://api.example.com/people/42'); // parsed data
const {data, etag} = await io.full.get('https://api.example.com/people/42'); // envelope
const body = await io.stream.get('https://api.example.com/big'); // ReadableStream

await io.post('https://api.example.com/people', {name: 'Ann'}); // objects go out as JSON
await io.put('https://api.example.com/people/42', person, {ifMatch: etag}); // 412, not a lost write
await io.del('https://api.example.com/people/42'); // io.delete / io.remove — same verb
```

## Entry points

The `exports` map is `{".": "./src/index.js", "./*": "./src/*"}` — a non-transforming wildcard, so
subpath imports carry the `.js` extension.

- `double-meh` — the shared, fully configured instance (default export) plus every named export.
- `double-meh/io.js` — `createIO()`, the bare pipeline with no services attached. Its default export is an instance with no transport registered either, so a consumer assembling its own must `registerTransport('fetch', fetchTransport)` and set `defaultTransport` before the first request; install services in the order `index.js` uses (track before cache, which shares the envelope track holds), each install call followed by its `attach()`.
- `double-meh/transports/fetch.js` — `fetchTransport`, the one core transport.
- `double-meh/services/{track,cache,retry,mock,bundle}.js` — `installTrack`, `installCache`, `installRetry`, `installMock`, `installBundle`.
- `double-meh/storage/{memory,fs,sqlite,cache-api,indexed-db,web-storage,opfs}.js` — cache backends: `memoryStorage`, `fsStorage`, `sqliteStorage`, `cacheApiStorage`, `indexedDbStorage`, `webStorage` (takes `store` — `sessionStorage` by default — and uses `name` as a key prefix, being the only backend with no container of its own), `opfsStorage` (origin private file system; bytes, no encoding, origin-pool quota; `keys()` opens every entry, and `createWritable()` on the main thread is Safari 26).
- `memoryStorage({maxBytes})` is unbounded by default; with a cap it evicts least-recently-used (a `Map` re-inserted on read), refuses an oversized entry with `QuotaExceededError`, and reports `storage.bytes`.
- `double-meh/storage/auto.js` — `autoStorage(candidates, {onPick})`: takes factories in preference order, keeps the first that survives a real set/get/keys/delete probe (key prefixed with a tab, so it cannot collide), memoized on first use, `chosen()` resolves to the winner, throws when none works rather than degrading to memory silently. Imports no backend itself.
- A `__doubleMeh.setup` callback returning a promise is awaited before any `inFlight` or `arrived` entry is drained, so a head script can `await import()` a cache backend and have the hand-over land in it; a rejecting callback is settled past, never wedging the prefetch.
- `double-meh/encoders/zlib.js` — `installZlibEncoders` plus `gzipEncoder`, `deflateEncoder`, `brotliEncoder`, `zstdEncoder` (br/zstd via `node:zlib`, kept out of browser bundles).
- `double-meh/sw.js` — `installSW`, `installChannel`, `SHARED_CACHE`, `CHANNEL` (page half of the Service Worker contract). On `{transport: 'sw'}`, `io.stream.*` negotiates a transferred `ReadableStream` body; other shapes keep the buffered default. URLs cross absolute — the worker cannot resolve a page-relative one.

- `io.cache.maxEntryBytes` caps a stored body (default `Infinity`); a quota failure sweeps expired entries, then evicts nearest-to-expiry, then drops the entry. Implicit caching never fails the request and emits `cache-skip`; `io.cache.save` rejects with `io.CacheFull` (`.key`, `.reason` of `quota`/`too-large`, `.name === 'QuotaExceededError'`), while a backend failing for another cause propagates unwrapped.
- Errors combine rather than vanish: an exhausted retry throws the last error with its type intact and an `AggregateError` of the earlier attempts on the cause chain; `io.cache.sweep`/`remove` and `fsStorage.clear` finish their loop and reject with an `AggregateError` of what they could not remove.

## Core API

`io` is callable and carries the verbs: `get`, `head`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete` (aliases
`del`, `remove`), `options`. Every verb is `(url, data?, options?)`; `url` may be a string, a `URL`,
or a reusable options bag acting as an endpoint descriptor.

Return shape is chosen by the namespace, never by an option:

- `io.get(url)` -> `Promise<T>` — the parsed data.
- `io.full.get(url)` -> `Promise<Envelope<T>>` — `{data, status, ok, response, headers}` plus lazy `etag`, `weak`, `lastModified`, `location`, `links`, `contentType`, `retryAfter`, `serverTiming`.
- `io.stream.get(url)` -> `Promise<ReadableStream>`; `io.stream.put/post/patch(url, options?)` -> `{writable, readable, response}` duplex.
- `io.records.get/post(url, data?, options?)` -> `AsyncIterableIterator<T>` — JSONL / `json-seq` framing.
- `io.sse(url, data?, options?)` -> `AsyncIterableIterator<SseEvent>` — reconnecting; `io.sse.reconnectDelay`.

Helpers: `io.update(target, fn)` (read -> apply -> conditional PUT, with 412 -> re-read -> retry),
`io.paginate(url)` (row iterator across pages), `io.getByIds(url, ids)` (falls back to POST past
`getByIds.urlLimit`, default 2000; `getByIds.overflow` is `'post'` by default or `'query'` for a cacheable overflow), `io.adopt(target, responseOrPromise)`, `io.run(target)`,
`io.toEnvelope(response, target)`, `io.makeKey(options)`, `io.buildUrl(options)`,
`io.makeVerb(method)`.

## Options

`{url, method, query, listSeparator, data, headers, signal, timeout, transport, fetch, accept, as,
decode, ifMatch, ifNoneMatch, fields, sort, expand, page, stream, bust, ignoreBadStatus, cache,
track, mock, retry, compress, bundle, idempotencyKey, force, onDownloadProgress, onUploadProgress,
meta}`

Notable:

- `as` — request body shaping: `'merge-patch'`, `'json-patch'`, `'json'`, `'ndjson'`, `'jsonl'`, `'text'`, `'csv'`, `'html'`, `'xml'`, `'form'`, `'octet'`.
- `io.bundle.register({url, host, match, method})` — select a bundler by `host` (parsed, lower-cased `URL.host`; string, array, RegExp, or predicate; an unparseable URL matches nothing) and/or by `match` (a string is a literal PREFIX, so it is not a host boundary — `'https://api.example.com'` also matches `https://api.example.com.evil.test`). Both narrow when both are given. Prefer `host` between APIs: a bundler fetches on the page's behalf and may reject a whole bundle over one URL it does not handle, so a stray part fails every request in that window. `io.bundle.url` is a catch-all — leave it empty with per-host bundlers. Client-side selection is routing; the bundler enforces.
- `io.query(url, criteria)` — RFC 10008 QUERY: a safe, idempotent read whose criteria are the body. Treated as a read throughout: tracked and cached like GET, keyed by `method + URL + accept + hash(body)`. No automatic downgrade to POST where a server rejects it; a 405 surfaces as `BadStatus`.
- `variant` — sets the body component of the key directly, for any verb. Needed where a body cannot be hashed (stream, `Blob`, `FormData`) and for telling two hand-overs to one URL apart. Unsafe verbs carry no body component by default, since nothing shares them; a safe verb whose body cannot be hashed opts out of track and cache rather than sharing a bodyless key.
- `decode` — `'json' | 'text' | 'blob' | 'arrayBuffer' | 'formData' | 'response'`, or a function. `'response'` returns the unread `Response` (the short form of `(await io.full(url)).response`) and always yields one, including every case that decodes to `undefined` — `204`/`205`, an absent body, `HEAD`/`OPTIONS`, and an inspected error status; like any `decode` override it opts the request out of `track`.
- `listSeparator` — how arrays serialize in the query. Unset/`null` = repeated keys (`?tags=a&tags=b`), the ambiguity-free default; a string joins (`','` -> `?tags=a,b`). `fields`/`sort`/`expand` default to `','` on their own.
- `retry` — `true`, a count, or `{retries, initDelay, force, nextDelay, continueRetries}`; `continueRetries` turns retry into polling.
- `cache` — `true`/`false` or `{ttl}`; `track` — `true`/`false`/`'wait'` (register interest without firing).
- `compress` — an encoder name, `true` for gzip, or an inline encoder function.
- `idempotencyKey` — `true` mints one key per logical operation, reused across retries.

## Services

Response-level middleware in a priority onion; each opts in per request (its own option wins) or by
`theDefault` (boolean or predicate). Cache and track are on by default for plain GETs.

- `io.track` — run-level GET dedup at the decoded-envelope level, plus `adopt`. Cancellation is refcounted: a caller's abort detaches only that caller; the wire aborts when the last waiter leaves.
- The hand-over is verb-agnostic by design and takes no view on semantics; in practice a non-GET hand-over is a read that does not fit a GET (a bundle request, a large search body, `QUERY`). A state-changing call is possible and runs on every page load whether or not the application asks for it.
- A hand-over target may be a `Request`, a `URL`, a string, or an options object; a `Request` contributes only method, URL and `Accept` (its own `cache`/`mode`/`credentials` never reach the key). A hand-over the cache will not keep (every non-GET, and a GET whose cache is detached or declines it) is held in memory when its response lands with no waiter, until one taker collects it or `io.track.retainMs` passes (default 60000, `0` disables) — never stored, distinct from caching. A hold is keyed, not payload-aware: the first matching call takes it whatever body it meant to send. Keys nobody handed over are untouched, so overlapping POST/PUT calls to one URL stay independent.
- A key reserved by `io.track.fly(target)` or already handed to `io.adopt(target, source)` is honored whatever the verb: the GET-only rule in `track.optIn` governs inferred dedup, not an explicit reservation, so a code-forward `POST`/`PUT`/`QUERY` hand-over resolves the application's matching call. Unreserved non-GET calls are never shared, the entry is consumed once, and only a GET hand-over is cached.
- `io.cache` reads server directives narrowly. Positive freshness is used (`max-age` > 0, a future `Expires`), precedence `cache: {ttl}` > server > `io.cache.defaultTtl`, switchable per call or globally with `fromHeaders` (default true). Negative forms (`no-cache`, `must-revalidate`, `max-age=0`) are ignored as the absence of a schedule. `no-store` routes the entry to `io.cache.volatile`, an always-memory tier, so it is cached for the page and never durable; reads/remove/sweep/clear span both tiers. `Vary` is identity, so it is obeyed; `Vary: *` blocks storage unless `cache: {vary: false}`, which also collapses variant keying for an application that handles variance itself. `s-maxage` is ignored (a page cache is private).
- `io.cache.storage` defaults to `autoStorage(defaultCandidates)` (`double-meh/storage/candidates.js`): in a browser IndexedDB, then the Cache API, then `sessionStorage`, then memory, each loaded on demand and trial-written before use; outside a browser, memory alone. Each rung is reached as `window.indexedDB` / `window.caches` / `window.sessionStorage`, so `window` is both accessor and gate: no CLI runtime defines it and a worker has `self`, where a bare `typeof indexedDB` check would accept Node's global `sessionStorage` or Deno's `caches`. Lazy, so a page that never caches never probes. On resolution it sets `io.cache.backend` and emits `cache-backend` `{backend, index, storage}`. Origin-scoped and named `double-meh`, so every instance in a page shares it.
- `io.cache.watch(promise)` registers cache work with `io.cache.idle()`; `io.adopt` uses it so a hand-over whose save has not started is still awaited.
- `io.cache` — app-governed cache: `storage`, `defaultTtl`, `remove(pattern)`, `clear()`, `sweep()`, `save()`, `idle()`. Honors `Vary`, revalidates with 304.
- `io.retry` — verb-safety-aware: `retries`, `initDelay`, `maxDelay`, `nextDelay()`.
- `io.mock(matcher, callback)` — serverless mocking through the real pipeline, so a mocked 503 really gets retried.
- `io.bundle` — batches GETs into one request to a bundler endpoint: `url`, `waitTime`, `maxSize`, `minSize`, `maxWait`, `streaming`, `writeThrough`, `register(config)`, `flush(name?)`, `submit(requests)`, `fly(targets)`. `streaming: true` (default false) asks for the `…bundle+jsonl` framing and resolves each waiter as its part arrives, in completion order; it costs server-side compression, so it is opt-in.

## Errors

`IOError` <- `FailedIO` <- `TimedOut`, and `IOError` <- `BadStatus`. A thrown `BadStatus` carries the
same envelope shape as a success, so error handling reads like success handling; `problem+json` is
already parsed into `error.data`. `isAbort(error)` classifies aborts.

```js
try {
  await io.get('https://api.example.com/missing');
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof io.BadStatus) console.error(error.status, error.data?.detail);
}
```

## Instances and extension points

The default export is one shared configured instance. `io.create()` gives an isolated equivalent;
`createIO()` from `double-meh/io.js` gives a bare pipeline.

`io.defaults(match?, bag)` registers scoped option defaults — the lowest merge layer, applied before
the endpoint descriptor and per-call options. Also `registerTransport`, `inspect.request(fn, match?)`,
`inspect.response(fn, match?)`, `registerData`, `registerMime`, `attach(service)`, `detach(name)`, and
the `on`/`off`/`emit` event surface.
